clue.text: Red hot sauce uses salt in Ascot recipe

indicators.note: the sailor is placed inside the rearranged letters of the racecourse name
a recipe is a way of mixing things up, so the letters of Ascot are reworked

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

explanation.surface: A fiery sauce features in a dish prepared for Royal Ascot.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is the Berkshire racecourse famous for Royal Ascot; 'recipe' turns its letters into a sauce mix, and the sailor goes in after the first letter. 'uses' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand of chilli condiment from Louisiana is the classic fiery red pepper sauce.

clue.text: Youth-leader leaves Mull of Kintyre on time, showing ornament

indicators.note: to mull is to turn over in the mind, here signalling that the letters are turned about

parts.note: the leading letter of the word youth is Y

explanation.surface: A young leader departs the Scottish peninsula on schedule with a decorative keepsake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes the Y out of the place name before 'Mull' rearranges it. The Mull of Kintyre is a headland in south-west Scotland, so 'Mull' looks like part of the place name, not a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cheap piece of jewellery or knick-knack is a decorative bauble.

clue.text: Can attack butter on the farm

parts.note: a billycan is a camping cooking tin, often just called a billy
to go at someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: A tin can goes for the butter in a farmyard scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attack' gives GO AT, two words that run together. The definition plays on 'butter' as one who butts, not the dairy spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A male goat butts with its horns, so it is a farmyard creature that butts.

clue.text: Begin work in Dorset town

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: Someone starts a job in a market town in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join: dorSET TOwn. Dorset is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To set to is an idiom for starting a task with energy.

clue.text: Else white rose variety

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters are rearranged into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Gardening talk about a cultivar of white rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' looks like a rose cultivar but signals rearranging WHITE ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in a different case or if not, synonyms as adverbs.

clue.text: Carrots can be blue, we hear, in Australia

definitions.text: Carrots can be blue, we hear, in Australia

parts.words: Carrots can be blue, we hear, in Australia
parts.note: Carrots is a nickname for someone with ginger hair, and Australians by contrast call such a person Bluey

explanation.surface: An odd horticultural rumour that Australian carrots come out blue.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests vegetables; in fact 'Carrots' is a nickname for a person with ginger hair, whom Australians call Bluey or Blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with ginger hair gets nicknames like Carrots, or Bluey down under.

clue.text: What experts know about boxers?

parts.note: experts are said to know the ..., and boxers fight inside a ring fenced by cords

explanation.surface: A question about the specialist knowledge of fight fans or dog breeders.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'know the ropes' means to be experienced; the ring around boxers is literally ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cords that enclose a boxing ring are also the idiomatic know-how of a seasoned hand.

clue.text: Sailors deal in packs of cards

explanation.surface: Seamen pass the time dealing cards from several packs.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half as a pack (deck) and what is dealt from it (hands).
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary seamen working on a ship's upper level; also the sets of cards dealt from a pack.

clue.text: Alcohol compound derived from trees

indicators.note: something derived from a source is made out of it, here a new word made by reordering the letters of trees

explanation.surface: A chemistry note that a certain compound comes from tree sap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'derived from' sounds chemical but signals rearranging TREES.
explanation.definitionFit: In organic chemistry this kind of compound forms when an acid reacts with an alcohol.

clue.text: Benin once showed house with outside light

indicators.note: the daylight word goes around the dwelling word, sitting outside it

parts.note: daylight, so light can stand for day
a house is a home

explanation.surface: A West African country exhibited a house lit from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with outside' wraps the light word around the dwelling. Dahomey became Benin in 1975, hence 'once'. 'showed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The West African republic was called by this former name until 1975.

clue.text: Fiord popular with the French before end of August

parts.note: something popular is said to be in
le is the French masculine word for the

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here of August

explanation.surface: A Norwegian fjord that is popular with French tourists before late summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' is a link joining the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiord is a narrow arm of the sea, and a creek or narrow sea arm is the same thing.

clue.text: Square-dancing for kids?

parts.note: a children's playground game of hopping between chalked squares, read as a dance over squares

explanation.surface: A question about square dancing classes for children.
explanation.walkthrough: Square-dancing is a folk dance; here it means hopping around chalked squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Children jump through numbered squares drawn on the ground in this playground game.

clue.text: Consoles principal committees

explanation.surface: Comforts are offered to the main boards of a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consoles' is the noun (instrument panels), not the verb meaning comforts.
explanation.definitionFit: Banks of keys on organs or computers are consoles; key means principal and boards means committees.

clue.text: But its eastern dishes can not be taken out

definitions.text: But its eastern dishes can not be taken out

parts.words: But its eastern dishes can not be taken out
parts.note: dishes means attractive women, and a sultan's wives were kept secluded, so they could not be taken out on dates, unlike a takeaway meal

explanation.surface: A complaint that an oriental restaurant does not do takeaways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishes' suggests food, but it is slang for attractive people; 'taken out' means escorted on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: The women's quarters of an Ottoman palace housed wives and concubines kept secluded.

clue.text: Unpleasant person tickled to death

explanation.surface: Someone nasty laughs themselves to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tickled' refers to catching a fish by stroking its belly by hand, which ends in its death; an 'old trout' is slang for a disagreeable person.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad-tempered old woman is called an old trout; the freshwater fish is famously caught by tickling.

clue.text: Trunk opened by Douanier reveals bottom drawer

indicators.note: the opening of the word trunk is its first letter

parts.note: Henri Rousseau, the French painter, was nicknamed Le Douanier for his job as a customs clerk

explanation.surface: A customs officer opens a trunk and finds items stored for a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link. 'bottom drawer' is British for linen and household goods a bride collects before marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of clothes and linen for married life is what the British call her bottom drawer.

clue.text: List of goods to come up with, by Circle Line

parts.note: to come up with an idea is to invent it
a circle is shaped like the letter O
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A shopping list made on a London Underground journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here the words split into O and RY. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stocktake is a complete itemised record of stock held.

clue.text: Chaps, sort of square, in waistcoats and robes

indicators.note: the men and square go inside the waistcoats

parts.note: in American usage a vest is a waistcoat
chaps are men
a T-square is a drafting tool shaped like a T

explanation.surface: Men of a fashionably square sort dressed in waistcoats and gowns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the chaps and the square inside the waistcoats; vest for waistcoat is American usage. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Priests' ceremonial garments worn during services are robes.

clue.text: Public beef consultant?

parts.note: beef is slang for a complaint, so this is an official the public consults with grievances

explanation.surface: A question about an adviser to the meat trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like meat but means a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: An official appointed to investigate citizens' complaints against public bodies.

clue.text: Fashion-houses art in Stowe, for example

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: Fashion houses display art at Stowe, the stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: Stowe is a famous English country house; here it is Harriet Beecher Stowe, writer of Uncle Tom's Cabin. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Harriet Beecher Stowe was a woman writer, an old term for a female writer.

clue.text: Officially appoint quarter for junior diplomat

parts.note: to attach someone is to assign them officially to a post
a quarter is a compass point, here east, E

explanation.surface: Officials appoint someone to a district for a lowly embassy role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy staff member with a specialist role, often junior in rank.

clue.text: Wooden-soled shoe for boats at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or disordered, so the letters of boats are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sailors wear clogs on boats at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits the boats but signals rearranging BOATS. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A clog carved from a single block of wood worn by peasants in France.

clue.text: Space for spectators Chester racecourse

clue.text: Jobs for king in news agency

indicators.note: the king goes inside the agency name

parts.note: TASS was the Soviet state news agency
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: Work assignments for a monarch in a press bureau.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Assigned pieces of work are duties or chores.

clue.text: Rapid writer

explanation.surface: A fast author.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is Jonathan Swift, author of Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast is a synonym of the first; the Irish satirist Jonathan Swift is the second.

clue.text: Jogger, say, goes round acre with the rest

indicators.note: the memory jogger surrounds the acre letter

parts.note: a memory jogger is an example of a prompt that reminds you

explanation.surface: A runner laps a field with the others in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jogger' suggests a runner but means something that jogs the memory. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over once a part is taken is what is left.

clue.text: Jack up for salary increase

explanation.surface: Push up pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack up' means to lift, or to increase a price; a pay rise is called this in American English.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift with a jack is to elevate; an increase in wages is the American term for a pay rise.

clue.text: Arouse fashionable low dog

parts.note: something fashionable is in
a cur is a mongrel, a low-bred dog

explanation.surface: A trendy mongrel stirs up feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring anger or debt on oneself is to provoke or bring it about.

clue.text: Standard in theatre

explanation.surface: A standard production in a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is the Criterion on Piccadilly Circus in London's West End. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A test or measure for judging is a standard; also a London West End playhouse.

clue.text: Stop that butterfly!

explanation.surface: A cry to halt a butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' is a punctuation mark, not a command; the butterfly is a European species with a white mark like this punctuation. 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctuation mark marking a brief pause; also an orange butterfly with a white comma-shaped wing mark.

clue.text: Feel warmth of the sun coming out — ecstasy!

indicators.note: the letters come out in a new order, rearranging the sun

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Delight as the sun breaks through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' rearranges THE SUN into ENTHUS, then E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To show eager excitement is to gush or be passionate.

clue.text: Unusual setting of garnets

indicators.note: a setting places stones in a new arrangement, so the letters of garnets are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jeweller remarks on an odd mounting of red gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' looks like a jeweller's mount but signals rearranging GARNETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd and out of the ordinary are synonyms.
